about: Every number and claim this lesson shows or says, with its source. Melbourne, Australia: after a builder terminated a homeowner's contract on 12 Feb 2024, he posted on a Facebook complaint page and, on 17 Feb 2024, a Punjabi-language TikTok naming the company and its two directors (about 220,000 views, shared via WhatsApp, comments saying the company was going into liquidation), left up until about July 2025 despite repeated requests. A County Court jury rejected his truth defences on several allegations; the company got $673,000; the directors' defamation claims first failed for lack of serious harm, won on appeal (Victorian Court of Appeal, August 2026, [2026] VSCA 191), and on 28 Oct 2026 each got $105,000; $883,000 in all, costs expected past $1 million. Amounts in Australian dollars. Both pages opened and read on Nov 26, 2026 in Todd's live chat (WebSearch, then WebFetch on the result's address). We name no person and no business. Not used: names, the page's name, the expert's quotes, the consumer-law question the court left open.

story.title: Viral TikTok complaint leaves homeowner facing $1 million-plus bill

gb.label: The Good Builder, Nov 9, 2026, on Singh v Singh Homes Pty Ltd [2026] VSCA 191

terminated: builder terminated the contract 12 Feb 2024 after disputes over payments, site attendance and workmanship (The Good Builder; SmartCompany: construction work and payments)
posts: 14 Feb 2024 a post on a Facebook complaint page; 17 Feb 2024 a Punjabi-language TikTok naming the company and its two directors (The Good Builder)
viewsNote: about 220,000 views, shared via WhatsApp (SmartCompany; The Good Builder)
comments: comments conveyed that the company was going into liquidation (SmartCompany; The Good Builder)
customersNote: the company said about 12 prospective customers abandoned plans (SmartCompany); said as the builder's account
calls: a director said he received around 40 to 45 calls about the video, including from overseas (SmartCompany); said as 'dozens of calls'
leftUp: left online until around July 2025 despite repeated requests for removal (SmartCompany; The Good Builder); said as 'well over a year'
jury: a County Court jury rejected truth defences to several allegations (SmartCompany; The Good Builder)
companyNote: $673,000 for injurious falsehood and misleading or deceptive conduct, largely lost business (SmartCompany; The Good Builder)
appeal: the trial judge first found the directors had not shown serious harm; the Victorian Court of Appeal overturned that in August 2026 (SmartCompany; The Good Builder: the directors won their appeal)
eachNote: Oct 28, 2026: $100,000 general plus $5,000 aggravated damages to each director (SmartCompany)
totalNote: $673,000 plus 2 x $105,000 (SmartCompany); Australian dollars (a Victorian court)
costsNote: legal costs and interest expected to push liability beyond seven figures (SmartCompany) / past $1 million (The Good Builder); no costs figure confirmed; said as 'expected to top a million'
